text:
ConocoPhillips fell 2.3% today after oil prices dropped sharply on renewed diplomatic efforts to end the Iran conflict. Yesterday saw reports of Iran's supreme leader and top security officials discussing conditions for a ceasefire, which sent both Brent crude (down from $116 to around $115) and U.S. crude lower. The stock had surged 4.5% just two trading days earlier when Middle East tensions peaked and Brent hit a six-month high; today's decline reverses much of that geopolitical premium.

The underlying tension for energy stocks right now is whiplash: prices spiked on escalation risk (Houthi attacks, Saudi infrastructure concerns, Trump's rhetoric about Iran manipulation), but any hint of de-escalation immediately erases those gains. With the stock up nearly 5% over two weeks despite today's pullback, the pattern suggests investors are betting on persistent tension rather than a stable resolution—but each diplomatic signal triggers a sell-off as traders lock in those temporary gains.
